sections.overview: This Brazilian coastal ray is now Hypanus marianae, formerly Dasyatis. The Izu stingray profile is another former Dasyatis species, now placed in Hemitrygon.
sections.identification: It is a small stingray, recorded to at least 31 cm disc width, with notably large eyes.
sections.habitat: It uses coral reefs, seagrass beds, sandy shores and estuaries at roughly 1–30 m depth.
sections.diet: Stomach studies found a benthic diet dominated by shrimps, other crustaceans and polychaete worms.
sections.behavior: It is a coastal benthic predator whose prey composition shifts with age.
sections.reproduction: Females have low fecundity, usually producing one pup; this limits recovery from fishing mortality.
sections.ecology: Endemic to Brazil, it is a mesopredator in shallow coastal benthic food webs.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as Endangered because intensive fishing and coastal habitat degradation threaten this low-fecundity ray.
